tagline: Across an old lake to the duck decoys.
intro: Out of Lovelock, the back country byway crosses what remains of Lake Lahontan on its twenty miles to Lovelock Cave. The old lake has gone. The cave kept duck decoys and baskets two thousand years, and it is known as the cradle of Great Basin archaeology.

Lovelock itself was founded with the building of the Central Pacific Railroad. When the railroad planned to tear down its wooden depot, the town took the building, moved it across Broadway Avenue and restored it. Shops lease it now.

moments.title: Lovelock depot
moments.text: Brackets and finials dress the wooden depot, moved across Broadway Avenue after the railroad proposed tearing it down.

moments.title: Lovelock Cave
moments.text: A self-guided nature trail explores the cave area where duck decoys and baskets survived for two thousand years.

practical: Portions of the byway may require a high-clearance vehicle.

sources.label: Bureau of Land Management, Nevada Byways
